title: Aegis Financial - Procurement + MSA/DPA Review
summary: Procurement/Legal review of Redwood MSA and DPA. Main topics: liability cap, indemnity, data residency, KMS/HSM support, SOC2 evidence, SLA levels and credits, onboarding timeline and pricing approvals. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share redline-ready MSA/DPA and SOC2 report, schedule technical onboarding POC, customer to route pricing to procurement and legal to provide redlines by 2025-08-21.
topics: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and data residency
Onboarding checklist and POC for Dedicated vs Hosted
next_steps: Alex to send editable MSA + DPA and SOC2 report link (by 2025-08-15)
Priya to schedule 2-hour technical POC for Dedicated throughput tests (tentative week of 8/25)
Karen to route pricing to procurement and share budget approval timeline (due 2025-08-20)
Devon to provide initial redlines for MSA/DPA (due 2025-08-21)
action_items: Alex Morgan - Share redline-friendly MSA + DPA and SOC2 (due 2025-08-15)
Priya Singh - Prepare POC plan and benchmark template (due 2025-08-18)
Karen Lee - Confirm procurement approval timeline and required PO process (due 2025-08-20)
Devon Price - Return legal redlines for MSA/DPA (due 2025-08-21)
Miguel Santos - Provide list of production traffic patterns for cost modeling (due 2025-08-19)
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-08-14
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Karen Lee (Aegis Procurement), Devon Price (Aegis Legal), Miguel Santos (Aegis VP Eng), Anita Rao (Aegis Cloud Sec)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE for Aegis. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Karen Lee: Karen here, procurement.
[00:12] Devon Price: Devon, legal.
[00:14] Miguel Santos: Miguel, VP Eng.
[00:16] Anita Rao: Anita, cloud security.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Priya, SE on the Redwood team.
[00:22] Alex Morgan: Great. The goal today is to walk through the MSA/DPA, call out any redlines, confirm SLA and onboarding steps, and align on pricing and timing. We'll leave time for questions.
[00:35] Karen Lee: Sounds good. From procurement perspective, we need to confirm host vs dedicated options, pricing bands, and PO process. Our finance team wants to understand the billing cadence.
[00:45] Alex Morgan: Totally — billing is monthly for hosted usage, reserved capacity is invoiced monthly based on committed units unless you want annual billing. We can support invoice-to-PO mapping, GL codes in invoice.
[00:58] Devon Price: On the MSA I have a few opens: liability cap, indemnity carve-outs for IP, and data handling clauses in the DPA. We've got a standard bank playbook and will want a 50k liability cap per year for SaaS vendors usually, is that something Redwood can accept?
[01:20] Priya Singh: I can chime technical implications — liability cap requests are commercial, but we do see enterprise customers negotiate. For dedicated/on-prem deployments some terms are easier to accept because of data isolation.
[01:35] Miguel Santos: From eng side, our big ask is key management: we need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption-at-rest and a documented key rotation policy. Also audit logs with token-level traces for model calls.
[01:50] Anita Rao: And we need SOC2 Type II evidence, penetration test summary, and the ability to have auditing access to logs for compliance. Also, DPA must have clear subprocessor list and data residency options, we operate in us-east for production and require EU residency for some PII flows.
[02:10] Alex Morgan: Understood. We'll share SOC2 and pentest artifacts under an NDA redaction path, and we support KMS integrations — we have a customer-managed KMS for both hosted and private options, and on Dedicated you can bring your own HSM in some regions. Data residency can be pinned by region at deploy time.
[02:30] Devon Price: On indemnity, we need to ensure carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct, but avoid overly broad indemnity to other third parties. Also curious about data deletion post-contract — DPA says 30 days, can you do 90?
[02:50] Priya Singh: Technically, we can support extended deletion windows; it impacts cache retention policies and backups. 90 days is doable with an explicit config. We do have support for purge requests and certified deletion reports.
[03:05] Alex Morgan: On the liability cap, we typically see a reciprocal cap tied to fees paid in prior 12 months or an agreed fixed cap for enterprise deals. If 50k is the starting ask, let's mark that as a customer redline and Alex/Legal will escalate internally.
[03:22] Karen Lee: Also our procurement needs to understand SLA credits. If SLA is 99.9% we need to understand how credits are calculated and if there's any uptime SLO for streaming responses. Latency is also a concern — our SLA should cover p99 for certain endpoints.
[03:40] Priya Singh: Our standard SLA for hosted endpoints is 99.9% availability, and we have per-route latency SLOs that can be agreed in the schedule. Credits are pro-rated percent-of-month credits calculated based on downtime windows. For dedicated we can offer higher SLOs with reserved capacity and a custom SLA.
[03:58] Miguel Santos: Are those credits the only remedy? Our legal likes exceptions but wants to make sure there are operational playbooks for incident response and on-call support levels.
[04:12] Alex Morgan: Typically yes, credits are primary remedy; we can discuss elevated support tiers for financial recourse but that's uncommon. We do provide incident post-mortems and have a 24/7 on-call for P1s depending on plan.
[04:26] Anita Rao: For security controls, we require SSO (SAML/IdP), RBAC, and fine-grained audit logging. Can you confirm SAML and SCIM provisioning?
[04:36] Priya Singh: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. RBAC with role definitions is in the console; API keys can be scoped per-model/route.
[04:48] Devon Price: Logistics for vendor onboarding — we have a standard security questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ). Will Redwood complete that? Also we'll need a copies of the MSA with change-tracking for our redlines.
[05:00] Alex Morgan: We will complete SIG-lite and provide the SIG/CAIQ answers. I'll attach editable MSA and DPA and a redline-friendly Word doc.
[05:08] Karen Lee: Pricing approval — our budget owners need a formal quote broken by hosted vs dedicated and an estimate for token-based consumption costs. We'll need TCO for 6 and 12 month scenarios.
[05:20] Priya Singh: We'll produce a pricing spreadsheet with assumptions and a baseline run-rate for your traffic profile. If you want Reserved capacity, we'll include committed discounts and burst pricing. Miguel, can you share expected qps and sequence-length distribution?
[05:32] Miguel Santos: We'll send typical traffic patterns and a sample spike profile. Mostly p95 latency sensitive for auth flows, and bulk batch embedding jobs overnight.
[05:42] Priya Singh: Great that's perfect for configuring cache and batching recommendations.
[05:48] Alex Morgan: A few timelines: procurement wants PO in early Sept ideally. If legal redlines are returned in two weeks we can get a countersigned MSA inside 3 weeks depending on redlines. Onboarding and POC for Dedicated could run 2-4 weeks after signature.
[06:05] Karen Lee: That timeline should work conditional on pricing approval. We'll aim to get internal approvals by 8/20.
[06:12] Devon Price: I'll try to return first-pass redlines by 8/21 but will flag anything critical earlier. Liability cap and data residency are top priorities.
[06:21] Anita Rao: On the DPA, for EU residency we need to ensure subprocessors are listed and that Redwood will only process EU PII in the EU region. Is that covered today or part of a work order?
[06:33] Priya Singh: We have region pinning for customer projects; we'll note that in the DPA schedule for data residency. Subprocessor list is maintained and we'll provide it.
[06:43] Miguel Santos: One technical Q — for Dedicated, do we get visibility into the underlying GPU types and can we request specific instance classes for latency?
[06:53] Priya Singh: Yes, Dedicated configs allow specifying GPU families. We can provide recommended instance profiles based on your p99 latency targets; we'll include kernel/quantization tradeoffs in the POC plan.
[07:05] Alex Morgan: Cool. Any blockers from anyone now?
[07:09] Karen Lee: Insurance certificate — we need proof of insurance, both general liability and cyber liability.
[07:16] Alex Morgan: We'll attach the COI and cyber liability limits to the packet.
[07:21] Devon Price: Can you confirm backup retention and whether Redwood will produce deletion certificates after termination?
[07:29] Priya Singh: Yes, we can produce deletion confirmation. Backups are stored per region and retention windows can be configured — we'll include specifics in the DPA schedule.
[07:40] Miguel Santos: For the POC, we need a few sample throughput numbers and a contact at Redwood for day-to-day ops during the run.
[07:48] Priya Singh: That will be me — I'll be the technical contact and set up a Slack channel and runbook for the POC.
[07:55] Alex Morgan: Ok recap and next steps: Alex to send editable MSA + DPA + SOC2 and COI by tomorrow (8/15), Priya to share POC plan and benchmark template by 8/18, customer to return legal redlines by 8/21, procurement to route pricing by 8/20.
[08:10] Karen Lee: Good recap. Also can you include a sample SLA schedule that shows 99.9% vs 99.95% credits table?
[08:18] Priya Singh: Yep we'll include a sample SLA schedule and an example credit calc.
[08:23] Devon Price: One more ask — can Redwood agree to a mutual audit clause limited to once per year and scoped to SOC2 controls, with reasonable notice?
[08:34] Alex Morgan: We'll take that back to legal. Many customers ask for mutual audit; we typically provide SOC2 reports and allow a third-party attestation, but we'll check the feasibility and document.
[08:45] Miguel Santos: Sounds good. Anything else?
[08:48] Anita Rao: Nothing more from security. Thanks.
[08:50] Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs.
[08:55] [Call ends]
notes: Customer prefers region-pinning for EU PII flows
Customer requests COI and cyber insurance docs
Pricing spreadsheet requested with 6/12 month TCO
